correctness.rationale: The cycle equations are equivalent to \(y+\varphi(y)=3\cdot2^{a-1}\). Writing \(y=2^cm\) with \(m\) odd reduces the problem to \(2m+\varphi(m)=3\cdot2^{a-c}\). For \(m>1\), an exact \(2\)-adic valuation argument forces \(\nu_2(\varphi(m))=1\), hence \(m=p^e\) with \(p\equiv3\pmod4\); factorization then forces \(p=3,e=2,a-c=3\). The converse is checked algebraically. A finite exhaustive replay through \(a=18\) agrees with the theorem but is not the proof.
